name: Atorvastatin + Ezetimibe
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Neither component needs a kidney dose adjustment: atorvastatin is eliminated in bile and is unaffected by kidney disease, and ezetimibe exposure rises only about 1.5-fold in severe kidney impairment. The Irish label sets no kidney adjustment. Muscle toxicity risk is driven by dose and interacting drugs. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: SmPC sets no kidney adjustment; pharmacokinetic data use creatinine clearance (CrCl ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m2). Bands shown on CrCl.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 10/10 mg once daily; titrate at intervals of 4 weeks or more up to 10/80 mg (SmPC).
No dose adjustment in kidney impairment (SmPC). Atorvastatin is unaffected by kidney disease; ezetimibe AUC about 1.5-fold higher at CrCl ≤30.

hd: No dose adjustment in the SmPC (atorvastatin unaffected by kidney disease). No dialysis-specific data.
pd: No dose adjustment in the SmPC; no PD data.
crrt: No data; usually continued or held per clinical context.
dialyzable: Not stated (both highly protein-bound; removal unlikely).
monitoring: Liver function tests before starting and periodically (reduce or stop if transaminases stay above 3 times the upper limit). Creatine kinase if muscle symptoms: do not start if CK is above 5 times the upper limit; stop if above 10 times, or above 5 times with symptoms (SmPC 4.4).
